purpose: BatchSilver contention-safe publication proof under a genuine rollback-transition old-task/new-task overlap, per ticket 05/ticket 11

overlap_measurement.note: Both tasks hydrated the canonical silver database from the same pre-test base version 0.7s apart (genuine concurrent read), then their publish windows overlapped for ~70s (genuine concurrent write) before either completed.

cik_scoped_reconciliation.method: SHA-256 of canonical (sorted, all-columns-cast-to-VARCHAR) rows for the target CIK, captured before task launch and after both tasks reached STOPPED
cik_scoped_reconciliation.result: identical row_count and semantic_sha256 for all 6 tables, before vs. after
cik_scoped_reconciliation.note: One duplicate-looking (cik, ticker) pair in sec_company_ticker (AAPL with/without exchange) is a pre-existing data characteristic unrelated to this test — confirmed identical between the before and after snapshot, so not introduced by the overlap.

conclusion: Two ECS tasks running different warehouse image digests (the exact pair used across this session's digest-restore rehearsal) published to the same canonical silver object for the same CIK with genuinely overlapping hydrate and publish windows. Neither publish was silently lost: two distinct sequential canonical versions were recorded, and the target CIK's data is byte-identical (via semantic digest) before and after. Ticket 11's contention-safe publication boundary held under a real rollback-transition-style overlap.
